saints.sourceTitle: Saint Peter, Bishop of Sebaste, in Armenia

summary.text: A brother of Saint Basil the Great and Saint Gregory of Nyssa, and a bishop at the Second Ecumenical Council. He is distinct from the Apostle Peter.
summary.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

saints.context: The Church's published hagiographic account is distinguished from independently established chronology. Unknown dates and circumstances are left unspecified.

blocks.text: His older sister Saint Macrina played an important part in raising him. The OCA life identifies the family relationship to the two Cappadocian bishops.

blocks.text: Saint Basil ordained Peter to the priesthood. Peter later became bishop of Sebaste, in Armenia, and attended the council at Constantinople in 381.

blocks.text: His conciliar participation places him among the bishops who opposed the teaching associated with Macedonius. His Orthodox commemoration is January 9.
